jobs.occupation: Associate Professorship at the Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research
jobs.description:
The Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research, Department of Psychology and Behavioural Sciences, Aarhus University, invites applications for Associate Professorship in social science alcohol and drug research, commencing 1 May 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research is an independent, interdisciplinary social science research centre. As an Associate Professor, you are expected to conduct high-quality research that strengthens the Centre’s research environment and contributes to the development of alcohol and drug research in Denmark. You will be expected to help strengthen the Centre’s international, including Nordic, research profile and collaborative activities within the field.

Candidates are expected to attract external research funding, publish in recognised academic journals and book series, teach at undergraduate and graduate levels, supervise PhD students, and have experience in, or shortly after appointment take responsibility for, leading research projects. There is also an expectation that you actively disseminate alcohol and drug research in a Danish context to practitioners, policymakers, and the general public. Furthermore, it is a requirement that you are based at the Centre on a daily basis and contribute actively and enthusiastically to its interdisciplinary research environment. Administrative duties will also be associated with the position.

Qualifications

Applicants with a social science research background in alcohol and drug studies and related areas will be preferred. Appointment as Associate Professor furthermore requires research and teaching qualifications equivalent to those typically achieved through a successful period of employment as an Assistant Professor although equivalent qualifications may also have been acquired through other means. To obtain permanent employment as an Associate Professor at Aarhus BSS, candidates must, prior to appointment, have completed the faculty’s supervision course and the faculty’s course in Online and Blended Learning offered by the Centre for Educational Development at Aarhus University. If these courses have not been completed prior to employment, appointment will be conditional upon their completion within five years.

About Us

At the Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research, we conduct social science research within the field of alcohol and drug studies. Our research projects focus on areas including treatment, prevention and harm reduction, policy, law enforcement, and recreational substance use. We study both legal and illegal substances. The Centre is interdisciplinary, and staff members have backgrounds in fields such as anthropology, psychology, sociology, criminology, and public health. Our aim is to establish and conduct research projects, provide teaching, disseminate knowledge about alcohol and drug problems, develop interventions, and collaborate with national stakeholders and international research institutions. For more information about the Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research, please visit www.crf.au.dk.

The Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research is part of the Department of Psychology, Aarhus BSS, Aarhus University. The Department of Psychology is one of six departments within Aarhus BSS, one of the University’s five faculties. Aarhus BSS brings together the core business and social science disciplines to reflect the close relationship between society and business. Aarhus University is ranked among the world’s top 100 universities, and Aarhus BSS and the Department of Psychology have obtained the prestigious AACSB and AMBA accreditations.

Further Information

For further information regarding the position, please contact: Bagga Bjerge, Director, Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research, Tel.: +45 22 35 19 89. Email: bb.crf@psy.au.dk

If you require assistance with uploading your application or have questions regarding the recruitment process, please contact: Charlotte Thomsen, HR-Coordinator. Tel.: +45 87 16 53 62. Email: Charlotte@au.dk.

The place of employment is: Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research, Bartholins Allé 9, 8000 Aarhus C, Denmark

Application deadline
12 January 2027

International applicant? 
Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information here:
https://internationalstaff.au.dk/relocationservice/

Please find more information about research opportunities at Aarhus University here: http://international.au.dk/research/

Terms of employment
Salary and terms of employment are governed by the Cirkulære om overenskomst for akademikere i staten  (in Danish). You will be employed as associate professor at base pay level 4–8 with additional supplements in accordance with the Cirkulære om protokollat om visse ansættelsesvilkår for videnskabeligt personale ved universiteter (in Danish).

The job content and qualification requirements are described in further detail in the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

Application procedure
When you apply for this position it is mandatory to attach the following:

• Application
• Curriculum Vitae. You are encouraged to declare any periods of leave without research activity, including, for example, maternity leave, since your research activities are assessed in relation to your actual research time
• Education (diploma for master's, PhD and possibly higher doctoral degree)
• List of publications (the enclosed publications must be clearly marked on the list of publications)
• Publications. Up to five publications can be included in the application. In the event of several authors the publications must be accompanied by a co-author statement concerning the applicant's share of the collaborative work with the consent of the co-authors. This template may be used for the purpose
• Teaching portfolio. The specific requirements regarding the documentation can be found here
 Materials which cannot be uploaded together with the application may be submitted in five copies to Aarhus BSS HR & PhD, Aarhus University, Bartholins Allé 16, DK-8000 Aarhus C.

Read more about how to apply for an academic post at Aarhus BSS here

The evaluation process
After the application deadline, an assessment committee is appointed. Please note that the assessment of applicants is based solely on the material received prior to the application deadline. For further information, see Guidelines for Assessment Committee, Aarhus BSS.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

About Aarhus University

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment for its 37,500 students, including PhD students, and has 9,000 employees (full-time equivalents) and an annual revenue of EUR 1.2 billion. Learn more at international.au.dk

Actona Group is on an ambitious transformation journey. As we continue strengthening our Customer Operations organisation, we are looking for a Customer Operations Manager to lead a team of approximately 10 dedicated employees.

In this role, you will be responsible for ensuring a consistently high-quality B2B customer experience across our customer portfolio while driving operational excellence, digital development, and team performance.

A key priority will be to develop and strengthen our digital customer entry points, making it easier for customers to interact with us while reducing manual work for the team. This is a role for someone who thrives on leading people, driving high-performance, and improving the way things are done. We are looking for a proactive leader who thrives in a changing environment, is motivated by creating results through others and who wants to take an active part in Actona Group's transformation journey.

• Continue to strengthen a culture of accountability, customer centricity, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

• Drive the development and adoption of digital customer entry points to simplify customer interactions and reduce manual handling, creating capacity for more proactive customer engagement.

You have a strong interest in digital development including AI and experience translating customer and operational needs into practical digital improvements. You see how simpler digital interactions can free up time for the team to build stronger customer relationships and support commercial opportunities together with Sales.

Most importantly, you are:

• A motivating and engaging leader.
• Thrives in a dynamic environment and remains focused and constructive during periods of change.
• Proactive and naturally inclined to take ownership.
• Comfortable leading through KPIs and performance management.
• Ambitious and eager to grow alongside the business.
Why Join Actona Group?

This is an opportunity to become part of a company with strong ambitions and a clear transformation agenda.

You will join an international environment where you can make a real impact on people, processes, performance, and customer experience. As Actona Group continues its transformation journey, we offer exciting opportunities for personal and professional growth for individuals who demonstrate ambition, ownership, and the ability to create impact through people and performance.

We are looking for someone with ambition, drive, and a desire to grow with the business. Someone who is excited by change, motivated by improvement, and eager to help shape the future of Customer Operations at Actona Group.

One sustains crawl throughput so that cost tracks value rather than volume. The other builds the shared foundations the rest of Siteimprove works through, so product lines reach content through common contracts rather than each solving it their own way. Pillar strategy is set with Seattle, nine hours behind you, and you are the leader on the ground who turns it into local decisions rather than waiting on it.

Your teams set the ceiling on what the rest of Siteimprove can build. Your goals follow from that — ingestion reliable enough that customers trust it, efficient enough that cost tracks value rather than volume, capable enough to feed our agentic products, and ready for the compliance bar our public sector customers require. You will use AI to build the platform that powers our AI products and stay close enough to the code to argue a design on its merits.

What we will be doing

• Decision Authority in Copenhagen: You are the decision-maker on the ground. Resolve in Copenhagen hours what would otherwise wait overnight. As engineering's voice in the group's trio, bring the constraints Product and UX have no way to see into scope conversations early enough to change them. Your director sets goals with you and discusses how you and the group are tracking against them.

• Platform Ownership: Own Content Platform's ingestion surface as a running business — availability, throughput, cost, and delivery predictability. Modernization is how you improve those numbers, not a separate program you report on. Our move to EKS is part of it. You decide which debt gets paid down and when and keep that trade-off in front of the trio.

• Architectural Direction: Own the constraints and the cross-team contracts your Technical Leaders design within: scheduling the crawl workload so cost tracks value rather than volume, moving ingestion onto event-driven services, and defining how the rest of Siteimprove consumes what we ingest. You will hold that direction with your senior engineers, because authority here is earned in design review.

• Delivery Under Pressure: Hold the delivery line when priorities move. Work arrives from outside the team continuously, and you will sequence so committed work reaches completion rather than stalling half-built. Align directly with peer engineering leaders and close the gaps at functions you depend on but don't manage.

• Measurable Impact: Define the KPIs these systems are judged by and hold your teams to them. You will prove the impact of what you prioritize in throughput, cost, and reliability rather than asserting it, and you will stop work that moves none of them.

• Growing Your Engineers: Own performance, career development, and compensation decisions for the group. Hand the Tech Vision and System Design for major initiatives to the engineers closest to the systems, and review rather than drive them.

• AI-Native Delivery: Use AI for engineering throughput, not just for product features. You will model the practice yourself: interpreting legacy code paths nobody documented, generating test coverage around behavior before you change it, and shortening the distance between a design decision and a working replacement

• Travel may be required; a valid passport is required

We want evidence of decisions you made rather than escalated, because waiting would have cost more than being wrong. This role also asks for a standing weekly overlap in your late afternoon, when the Seattle day begins, so that the conversation with your director is a working one.

• Leadership Through Leaders: 10+ years managing engineers, including senior technical leaders whose designs you reviewed rather than produced, and whose scope you expanded rather than absorbed.

• Architectural Judgment: A track record of moving established services onto cloud-native infrastructure and of designing interfaces other teams build on. What matters is having lived with both long enough to know which decisions held and which leaked.

• Three offices: Copenhagen, London and Iași, with customers across more than 15 countries.

**THE OPPORTUNITY

**We are looking for a DevOps Engineer to join our Platform team and help us scale infrastructure, CI/CD, and observability across our growing backend ecosystem.

You will work alongside our senior platform engineers on our Kubernetes-native stack, taking ownership of real infrastructure from early on. This is a role where you'll learn by building: our environment is modern and opinionated, and you'll be running production infrastructure for financial institutions, not sandbox projects.

We are looking for someone who is genuinely curious about how systems work, comfortable being new to things, and eager to grow fast in a high-bar environment.

**What You Will Be Doing

**

• Infrastructure as Code: Build and maintain our AWS infrastructure using Terraform/Terragrunt, starting with well-scoped modules and growing into larger architectural work.

• Collaboration: Work closely with backend engineers and security stakeholders, applying cloud security best practices with AWS-native tooling.

**What We Are Looking For

**

**OUR TECH INTERESTS

jobs.occupation: Management Consultants in Supply Chain Planning – Graduates 2027
jobs.description:
Job description

We're looking for talented and curious graduates who want to start a career in management consulting at the intersection of deep functional expertise and digital planning solutions.

What you’ll do

In this role, you’ll be joining a nerdy team that designs and delivers optimal supply chains by combining best-in-class processes with leading digital solutions. Every day, we help clients transform their planning processes in demand, supply, and inventory optimisation across the value chain and planning horizons.

You’ll be working on a wide range of projects. Depending on your personal journey and development goals, your role in a project could include:

• Design and implement planning excellence: Apply advanced concepts in forecasting, demand and supply planning, S&OP/IBP, inventory optimisation, and operational planning to build robust, end‑to‑end planning processes.

• Enable adoption and capability building: Train stakeholders and facilitate client workshops to co-create designs, refine processes, and embed continuous improvement.

• Translate requirements into actionable processes: Convert business needs into well-defined process designs and implementation plans – with clear governance, data, and decision flows.

• Guide digital planning transformations: Advise clients on solution architecture and roadmaps for SAP IBP and other leading platforms from concept to configuration and adoption.

• Deliver measurable impact: Execute projects that optimise planning tools and processes, strengthen performance management, and build organisational capabilities that sustain excellence.

• You’re excited to live a year in Copenhagen to immerse yourself in our strong Implement culture while working in an international team and to build a broad network at Implement.

If this sounds like the kind of nerdery you would like to dive deep into, you’ll feel right at home in our team.

Please note that for the first year, you’ll be employed in our Copenhagen office, Implement’s HQ, before joining the Aarhus office.

What you’ll bring

As our new team member, you’ll be working at the forefront of supply chain transformation – integrating digital enablers with core business functions to create end-to-end impact, from strategy and design to implementation and adoption.

To be a great fit, you hold – or are about to complete – a master's degree in a relevant field such as engineering, supply chain, operations research, or business analytics, with strong academic results to show for it.

On top of that, we’re looking for someone who meets most of the following criteria:

• Relevant experience: Ideally, you’ve applied supply chain concepts through an internship, student role, or thesis project.

• Project-driven and adaptable: You enjoy working in a project-based setting, managing timelines, stakeholders, and changing priorities.

• Interest in digital tools: Ideally, you have exposure to SAP (e.g., SAP IBP) or other digital planning platforms or you are interested in building expertise in digital planning solutions.

• Analytical problem-solver: You love turning complex problems into clear insights and actionable solutions.

• Structured communicator: You can structure and deliver compelling presentations and workshops in English (proficiency in another European language is considered a plus, but not a requirement).

Supply chains are becoming one of the most strategically important – and technically complex – areas in business. If you want to be at the sharp end of that, join our team where curiosity is rewarded, diverse perspectives are valued, and where you will make an impact from day one.

What we offer

At Implement, a healthy, dynamic, and collaborative environment always comes first. You'll become part of a fast-growing, entrepreneurial Scandinavian consultancy that gives you the space to grow, lead, and innovate while creating real results for our clients.

• Build deep functional expertise: develop mastery across demand planning, supply planning, inventory optimisation, S&OP/IBP, and digital planning tools with ownership of end-to-end planning transformations.

• Hands-on from day one: work on client projects immediately, side by side with experienced consultants who elevate your strategic thinking and methodological rigour.

• Continuous development: get access to an ambitious internal training programme with keynotes, workshops, certifications, and mentoring to accelerate your professional and personal growth.

• High-trust culture: enjoy autonomy, support, and a flat hierarchy in a team that shares knowledge freely and continuously raises its standards.

• An exciting start to your career: Feel the energy and atmosphere at our Copenhagen HQ for one year, joining a cohort of international graduates. Build a community and engage in a steep learning programme into the world of supply chain planning before you move on to the Aarhus office.

Make your next move matter.

How to apply

Please include your CV, a cover letter, and your GPA for both your BSc and MSc.

Start date for this position flexible, either winter 2026/2027 or September/October 2027 in Copenhagen.

About Implement

Implement Consulting Group (founded 1996) is an international management consulting firm with 1,900+ employees. Headquartered in Copenhagen, we have 12 offices across the Nordics, the DACH region, and the United States, making us one of the largest European consultancies. We support organisations in delivering sustainable strategic, commercial, and operational transformations. To help our clients succeed with their most critical change initiatives, we aim to attract, develop, and promote the best talent by creating a unique, collaborative learning environment where people can follow their passion, shape their own careers, and choose their own leaders.

**About Sedna:

**Sedna is at the forefront of revolutionising global trade, serving as the North Star for businesses navigating the complexities of international commerce. Our AI-powered platform is designed to make global trade more efficient, transparent, and sustainable. As we continue to grow and innovate, we are looking for exceptional talent to join our journey and contribute to our mission of transforming global trade.

You can find out more about us on our website: https://sedna.com/

**Role Snapshot

****Scope

**Owns a named portfolio of Premier and Strategic accounts globally. Co-owns renewals and expansion commercially with the AE. Owns the customer relationship, account health, success plan execution, and ensuring the customer is in the right place before the renewal conversation happens; Sales owns the close.

**Autonomy

**Operates independently with minimal management oversight. Escalates to Head of Customer Success on strategic or genuinely unusual situations only.

**Influence

**Directly shapes retention and growth outcomes on Sedna's highest-value accounts. Executive-level relationships and QBR ownership mean this role has material impact on revenue.

**Team

**Sets the standard for account management practice across the CS function. Acts as a reference point for regional CSMs on complex account situations.

**Role Overview

**The Enterprise Customer Success Manager owns Sedna's most commercially significant customer relationships. This is a senior, largely autonomous role for someone who is equally comfortable running an executive-level conversation and building the account infrastructure, success plans, health monitoring, renewal strategy, that makes that conversation credible.

The portfolio spans Premier and Strategic accounts globally. These are customers with high ARR, high complexity, and in many cases, long relationships that carry both genuine opportunity and genuine risk. The job is to hold those relationships well, act on signals before they become problems, and surface and progress commercial outcomes in partnership with Sales.

This is not a role that fits someone who needs clear direction on what to do next. The expectation is that you read the account, form a view, and act on it. The Head of Customer Success is there for strategic decisions and unusual situations, not routine account management.

**Key Responsibilities

****Account Ownership

**

• Own a named portfolio of Premier and Strategic accounts. Know them well enough that no renewal, no escalation, and no expansion conversation comes as a surprise.

• Build and maintain executive-level relationships. The relationship should not depend on the product working perfectly; it should be strong enough to hold when it does not.

• Produce and execute success plans tied to customer outcomes, not just product usage metrics. Plans should reflect what the customer is trying to achieve and how Sedna is contributing to it.

• Run QBRs with commercial framing. A QBR should advance the relationship and the commercial position, not just report on the quarter.

• Maintain deep product knowledge across Sedna Email, Prefix, and VMS. You are not delivering training, but your commercial conversations need to be grounded in a genuine understanding of how customers are using the product and where they are not.

**Retention and Renewal

**

• Monitor account health continuously and act on risk signals before they become churn conversations. If a customer is at risk, the Head of Customer Success should hear about it from you, not from the customer.

• Co-own the renewal conversation with the AE. Own the preparation, the relationship context, and the customer's readiness to renew; Sales owns the close.

• Escalate renewal risk early, with a clear view of what is driving it and what the options are.

**Growth and Expansion

**

• Identify and progress expansion opportunities in collaboration with the AE. This means having enough commercial awareness to spot the signal and enough credibility with the customer to explore it.

• Bring the Head of Customer Success into complex or large deals at the right moment, not after the conversation has already been shaped.

**Cross-functional Coordination

**

• Coordinate training delivery through Education. You are not responsible for delivering training; Education owns that. Your job is to ensure the right training reaches the right accounts at the right time.

• Work with the Programme Manager to ensure smooth onboarding for new accounts entering the portfolio.

• Provide context to Education Specialists before training sessions on Premier and Strategic accounts, so delivery is appropriately calibrated.

• Partner with Support and Product to close feedback loops and ensure customer insights are informing the right internal conversations.

**About You

**

• Significant experience managing complex, high-value B2B accounts at a senior level, with a track record of holding executive relationships and co-owning commercial outcomes alongside Sales.

• Strong executive presence and the ability to hold a relationship through difficult conversations, not just good ones.

• A background in shipping, maritime operations, or global trade is strongly preferred. Sedna serves some of the world's largest maritime businesses, and candidates who understand how those organisations operate will be better placed to build credible, lasting relationships with them.

• Commercially fluent: able to read a renewal situation, understand what is driving it, and act with appropriate urgency without waiting to be asked.

• Clear, structured communicator in writing and in person, comfortable presenting to senior stakeholders and leading commercial conversations.

• Familiarity with Salesforce or equivalent CRM. Experience with tools such as Mixpanel or Snowflake is an advantage.

**What Success Looks Like

**

• A portfolio where no renewal, escalation, or expansion conversation comes as a surprise, because you have been managing the signals well in advance.

• Executive relationships on Premier accounts that are strong enough that customers would describe you as genuinely useful, not just present.

• Net Revenue Retention at or above target, with a clear understanding of what drove the result in both directions.

• Expansion pipeline contribution in partnership with Sales, with opportunities identified and progressed rather than waited for.

• Customer insights flowing consistently into QBRs, product feedback, and internal planning.

**Directional KPIs

**

• Net Revenue Retention on portfolio

• Logo retention rate on portfolio

• Expansion ARR generated

• Renewal on-time rate

• QBR completion rate against plan

• Time to escalation on at-risk accounts (faster is better)

• Executive relationship health, qualitative, assessed quarterly by Head of Customer Success

• Training coordination rate: proportion of accounts receiving at least one Education touchpoint per quarter

**Our Values:

**Finally, culture is important to us, so we also look for candidates who share our values:

**Stay Ahead, Stay Agile

**

• We don’t just adapt-we anticipate change and act with confidence.

• Curiosity, data, and customer insights help us stay ahead of the curve.

• We embrace challenges as opportunities and remain resilient under pressure.

• By staying open to new ideas and ways of working, we lead the future.

**Execute With Focus

**

• We turn strategy into action, delivering measurable results that matter.

• Every initiative counts-discipline and ownership drive business impact.

• We make smart decisions with speed, balancing pace and precision.

• Clear priorities keep us focused on what moves the needle.

**Work Together, Win Together

**

• Collaboration is our superpower-we succeed as one team, internally and with customers.

• We co-create solutions, seek feedback, and build the future of the OS together.

• Strong relationships are built on trust, respect, and shared goals.

• By aligning across teams and with customers, we unlock greater impact.

Do you want to build a new repair and service capability for Weibel's radar systems

At Weibel, we develop and produce advanced radar systems for customers across the world. As our installed base continues to grow, so does the need for a dedicated capability that can provide our customers with efficient and consistent support when their radar systems require spare part replacement, repair or system updates.

We are therefore establishing a new Repair & Service function within Aftermarket, covering both our Instrumentation and Surveillance radar systems. The ambition is to build a strong, independent capability that brings the competencies, team and processes together in one dedicated workshop.

Today, these activities draw on resources from Production and Field Service. By bringing the responsibility together we establish a specialized function within Aftermarket to improve turnaround time for our customers and enable Production and Field Service to focus on their core responsibilities. You will play a key role in turning that ambition into a strong, self-sufficient function.

Build the function from the ground up

You will report to our Aftermarket Director and take the lead in establishing and developing the new Repair & Service function.

You will shape the workshop, build the team and competencies and establish the processes needed to handle spare part replacements, repairs and system updates efficiently across our radar portfolio. You will have the opportunity to build your own area of responsibility and set the direction for how the function develops as it grows.

A strong customer perspective will be central to the role. You will take responsibility for the complete repair journey, from the moment a need is reported until the radar or component is repaired, updated and ready to return to operation. Short turnaround times, high quality and clear communication will be key measures of success.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Establishing the new Repair & Service workshop, including the physical setup, equipment and workflows

• Building and developing the team and the technical competencies needed to support our radar systems

• Establishing efficient processes for spare part replacement, repair, system updates and testing

• Leading and developing the team and setting clear direction and priorities as the function grows

• Developing the spare parts setup needed to support an efficient Repair & Service operation together with Production and Warehouse

• Building strong collaboration with Production, Field Service and relevant technical functions across Weibel

• Using operational insights to continuously improve quality, turnaround time and the customer experience

Your first three priorities

When you join, your first focus will be to turn the ambition into a functioning Repair & Service capability:

• Understand the complete Repair & Service flow: Get close to the cases we handle today and understand the journey from the customer request until the radar or component is ready to return to operation. This will give you the foundation to identify the capabilities and processes the new function needs.

• Build the team and the workshop: Bring the right competencies together and establish the physical setup, tools and ways of working needed for the function to increasingly handle cases independently.

• Build first-hand knowledge of our radar systems: Work hands-on with current repair cases to understand our systems, typical faults and the technical capabilities your team needs to develop.

Your profile

You are a hands-on technical leader who is motivated by building something new and making it work. You enjoy creating structure where the path is not yet fully defined and know how to turn technical expertise into a strong team and a well-functioning operation.

You understand what it takes to troubleshoot, repair and test complex technical systems and can move comfortably between technical challenges, leadership and cross-functional collaboration.

We imagine that you bring:

• A relevant technical background within electronics, electrical or mechanical engineering, or equivalent practical experience

• Hands-on experience with troubleshooting, repair and testing of advanced electronic, instrumentation or comparable technical systems

• Experience leading and developing technical specialists

• Experience establishing, developing or scaling a workshop, service or repair function

• A structured approach to processes, quality and continuous improvement

• Understanding of spare parts and material flows

• Strong communication skills in Danish and English

• Most importantly, you have the drive to take ownership and build a new function into a strong capability

Contact and application

Please apply through our website using the Apply button.

If you have any questions, you are very welcome to contact our Aftermarket Director, Jakob Brade, at JABR@weibel.dk.

The deadline for applications is December 6, 2026.

Please be aware that employment requires a criminal record with no remarks and the ability to obtain security clearance.

We look forward to hearing from you.

Become part of a Danish company

Weibel Scientific A/S is a Danish-owned engineering company experiencing strong growth. We develop and manufacture high‑technology radar systems for use in areas such as space research, aviation, defense, and the protection of critical infrastructure. We are a world leader in the development of Doppler radars and, since our establishment in 1977, we have delivered more than 4,500 state‑of‑the‑art radar systems to over 40 countries.

Our headquarters are located in Allerød and employ nearly 600 people.

At Weibel, you can look forward to an exciting and challenging position in a dynamic and forward‑looking company with in‑house production and advanced technological development.

Read more about us on our website.

Develop physics-based wind and solar models and the Python software that brings them into daily use in energy trading.

The role

You will develop physics-based models of wind and solar production and build the Python software that puts them into reliable daily operation. Your work will support data validation, pricing, and hedging across our client business.

Over time, you will become the go-to person for asset modelling, taking ownership of model quality, and ensuring that consistent, traceable assumptions underpin our pricing and hedging decisions.

The team

The Pricing team develops and operates the models and analytical infrastructure used to evaluate deals and manage risk across our client business. We focus on making results reliable, traceable and useful for the decisions they support.

You will work alongside a software developer, quantitative developers and pricing analysts, while collaborating closely with colleagues in Forecasting, Portfolio Management and Client Success.

Your responsibilities

• Develop, validate and maintain physics-based wind and solar models, translating weather data and asset characteristics into expected production.

• Validate historical production data and distinguish underlying production potential from the effects of outages, curtailment and trading decisions.

• Build reusable Python components to calculate and store production estimates and expected volumes, ensuring traceability and reproducibility.

• Develop, test, deploy and operate Python models and supporting software, including monitoring, troubleshooting and maintenance.

• Develop and maintain day-ahead and intraday renewable asset hindcasts used in pricing.

• Work with our Forecasting team to incorporate in-house weather data and forecasting methods into our asset models.

• Assess external production indices against our models and document the assumptions behind the analysis.

Our asset models are the foundation for how we price renewable energy contracts and estimate the volumes we hedge in the market. We are looking for someone who takes ownership of their models, challenges the status quo and works closely with colleagues to turn theory into practice.

René Meklenborg Miltersen Slot

Manager, Pricing

What we are looking for

You combine expertise in both wind and solar production modelling with strong Python skills and experience taking software into production. You take ownership of model quality and reliability, challenge assumptions and assess whether more complex models add practical value given the uncertainty involved.

We will help you develop your knowledge of pricing, hedging and energy markets. Previous experience in these areas is welcome but not required.

We expect you to have

• A Master’s degree in engineering, physics, renewable energy or a related field.

• Several years of relevant experience in renewable asset modelling, energy yield assessment or a related technical role.

• Hands-on experience with reanalysis data, weather data and measured production time series.

• Solid experience modelling wind production, including turbine power curves and wake effects.

• Solid experience with PV performance modelling and the main drivers of solar production.

• Strong Python skills and experience developing, testing, deploying and operating models or analytical software in production.

• Experience using AI tools in daily coding, analysis or modelling, with a critical approach to reviewing and validating their outputs.

• The ability to communicate technical results clearly and collaborate across technical and commercial teams.

Advantageous experience

• Experience with historical weather forecasts, hindcasts or forecast verification.

• Experience combining physical models with statistical methods to improve production estimates.

• Familiarity with energy markets, PPA pricing or portfolio hedging.

What we offer

• Ownership of our renewable asset modelling capability, with a direct impact on commercial performance.

• The opportunity to combine renewable energy engineering, Python development and quantitative modelling in power markets.

• Hands-on modelling of real wind and solar assets using weather data and measured production.

• Close collaboration with developers, analysts, forecasters and portfolio managers.

• A strong technical environment, with room to shape our models and the analytical services around them.

• Competitive salary and attractive employment terms.

Interested?

If you bring expertise in wind and solar modelling and experience deploying and operating Python software, we would like to hear from you.

Want to know more?

Feel free to reach out if you have any questions about this opportunity

René Meklenborg Miltersen Slot

Manager, Pricing

jobs.occupation: Associate Director, Global Drug Safety & Pharmacovigilance Physician
jobs.description:
At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**The Role

**This role provides medical oversight of product safety, including adverse event review, ongoing safety surveillance, and management of emerging safety issues. Responsibilities include safety input to clinical and regulatory deliverables, aggregate reporting, safety committee oversight, cross-functional collaboration, and ensuring regulatory compliance and inspection readiness.

**Responsibilities

**

• Perform medical review of Adverse Events reports for Genmab products.

• Perform ongoing surveillance of safety data from Genmab clinical trials.

• Ensure handling of safety issues.

• Perform medical review and provide input to e.g., Trial Protocols and amendments, Trial Reports, Trial plans, eCRFs/CRFs, TMFs, Investigator’s Brochures, Subject Informed Consent, Development Safety Update Reports, Integrated Safety Summaries, scientific articles, and medical reviews.

• Prepare aggregated reports and safety summaries in accordance with regulatory requirements.

• Responsible for the establishment and management of external Data Monitoring Committees (DMCs)

• Chair and manage Genmab Safety Committees

• Conduct training of Genmab employees, CROs and Investigators

• Member of Clinical Management Teams (CMTs), Compound Development Teams (CDT) and Compound Strategy Teams (CST) and contribute to multidisciplinary project groups and provide input to clinical development programs.

• Interact with safety and clinical CROs and perform sponsor oversight activities.

• Collaborate with external experts and partners.

• Contribute to multidisciplinary project groups.

• Ensure compliance with regulatory guidelines and internal procedures in order to be prepared for audits and inspections.

• Participate in audit and inspection activities as relevant

**Requirements

**

• Medical degree (MD or equivalent) with relevant clinical experience; oncology or hematology experience preferred.

• 5 - 8 years of experience in pharmacovigilance, drug safety, or clinical development within the pharmaceutical/biotechnology industry.

• Demonstrated experience in adverse event medical review, safety surveillance, signal evaluation, benefit–risk assessment, and aggregate safety reporting.

• Experience providing medical safety input to clinical trials and regulatory deliverables, including protocols, Investigator’s Brochures, informed consent documents, DSURs, clinical study reports, and integrated safety summaries.

• Strong knowledge of global pharmacovigilance and clinical development requirements, with experience supporting Safety Committees/DMCs, regulatory submissions, audits, and inspections.

• Strong medical judgment, leadership, and communication skills, with demonstrated ability to collaborate across functions, CROs, external partners, and regulatory stakeholders.

• Experience executing processes/projects in own area (e.g. guidance documents as per intl. regulations & reporting requirements; preparation of post-marketing spontaneous and clinical trial safety assessments; regulatory submissions; safety case processing; PV data systems; safety data base systems and the report generation)

• Experience working with FDA/EMA/PMDA/ICH requirements, good clinical practices, and pharmaceutical clinical development

• Experience guiding team members around complex issues

For US based candidates, the proposed salary band for this position is as follows:

$200,000.00---$300,000.00

The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Also, certain positions are eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

When You Join Genmab, You’re Joining a Culture That Supports Your Physical, Financial, Social, And Emotional Wellness. Within The First Year, Regular Full-time U.S. Employees Are Eligible For

• 401(k) Plan: 100% match on the first 6% of contributions

• Health Benefits: Two medical plan options (including HDHP with HSA), dental, and vision insurance

• Voluntary Plans: Critical illness, accident, and hospital indemnity insurance

• Time Off: Paid vacation, sick leave, holidays, and 12 weeks of discretionary paid parental leave

• Support Resources: Access to child and adult backup care, family support programs, financial wellness tools, and emotional well-being support

• Additional Perks: Commuter benefits, tuition reimbursement, and a Lifestyle Spending Account for wellness and personal expenses

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on role will be provided during the recruitment process

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

Please note that if you are applying for a position in the Netherlands, Genmab’s policy for all permanently budgeted hires in NL is initially to offer a fixed-term employment contract for a year, if the employee performs well and if the business conditions do not change, renewal for an indefinite term may be considered after the fixed-term employment contract.
